integrity: The proof reconstructs the projective fixed-point calculation and invariant function field directly from Wu's defining equation and smoothness discriminant, then uses tame quotient theory and Riemann--Hurwitz. No finite experiment, numerical approximation, or unproved classification is used.
scientific limitations: The isogeny and rational two-torsion formulation requires a rational point chosen as origin; without one, the unconditional conclusion is the fixed-point-free degree-two etale quotient of genus-one curves. The result identifies one canonical quotient but does not classify all isogenies or torsion. A closely related 2026 source on a different characteristic-uniform family was available only at abstract level during comparison.
title: A canonical 2-isogeny on Wu's symmetric QRT biquadratic
